convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom() to load 'StochasticDiff' custom indicator, depends on external .mqh libraries (TradeAlgorithms.mqh, SmoothAlgorithms.mqh) for trade execution and smoothing algorithms, has custom money management with multiple margin modes

derived_values.name: TimeShiftSec - timeframe duration in seconds for signal timing
min_rates_total - minimum bars required for indicator calculation

other_exits: Buy close triggered when StochasticDiff[1]>StochasticDiff[2] (downturn detected)
Sell close triggered when StochasticDiff[1]<StochasticDiff[2] (upturn detected)

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MMMode=LOT means fixed lot size of MM=0.1; other modes (FREEMARGIN, BALANCE, LOSSFREEMARGIN, LOSSBALANCE) use MM as percentage of respective margin base

custom_logic_notes: Entry uses 3-bar comparison of single StochasticDiff buffer: Value[1]<Value[2] (upturn) + Value[0]>=Value[1] (current confirms) for buy; Value[1]>Value[2] (downturn) + Value[0]<=Value[1] (current confirms) for sell. When SignalBar=0, signals are recalculated on every tick instead of only on new bars. BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/SellPosClose/BuyPosClose booleans act as gate switches to independently enable/disable each direction's entry and exit. Signal time passed to trade functions uses SERIES_LASTBAR_DATE + TimeShiftSec for timing-based order management.
python_conversion_notes: The StochasticDiff custom indicator must be reimplemented in Python - it applies a second smoothing (T3 by default) over standard Stochastic values. The TradeAlgorithms.mqh library provides BuyPositionOpen/SellPositionOpen/BuyPositionClose/SellPositionClose functions with built-in position checking, money management across 5 modes (LOT, FREEMARGIN, BALANCE, LOSSFREEMARGIN, LOSSBALANCE), and deviation handling - these must be reimplemented. SmoothAlgorithms.mqh provides GetStartBars() and the T3/other smoothing implementations. The signal logic compares 3 consecutive values of the smoothed stochastic: bar[1] vs bar[2] determines direction, bar[0] vs bar[1] confirms entry. SL/TP are in points (1000/2000) not pips - need to verify if digit adjustment is needed for 5-digit brokers (no explicit adjustment found in code).
